babble.description: A busy room: six other Kokoro voices reading the unrelated everyday texts below at once, at equal level, each looped from its own random starting point
texts: The forecast for the weekend looks mixed. Saturday starts bright, with a light wind from the west, but clouds build through the afternoon and there may be a shower or two by the evening. Sunday should be drier and a little warmer, so if you were planning to walk along the river or visit the market, that is probably the better day for it.

For the bread, mix the flour, the salt and the yeast in a large bowl, then add the warm water a little at a time until the dough comes together. Knead it for about ten minutes, until it is smooth and springs back when you press it. Leave it somewhere warm until it has doubled in size, shape it gently, and bake it until the bottom sounds hollow when tapped.

Starting next month, the early train will leave the main station ten minutes later than it does now, and the last train in the evening will stop at every station on the line. The bus that meets the train at the bridge will wait for it if it runs late. New timetables are on the website and on the boards by the ticket office.

The tomatoes did well this year, but the beans were slow, probably because of the cold start to the season. Next spring I want to move the herbs closer to the kitchen door, build a second compost bin behind the shed, and try a row of sunflowers along the back fence where the light is best in the afternoon.

It was a close match all the way through. The home side scored early from a corner, the visitors equalised just before half time, and for most of the second half neither team could find a way through. Then, with only a few minutes left, a long pass over the top found the winger, who cut inside and curled it into the far corner.

The library is open late on Thursdays, until eight, and on Saturday mornings. You can return books at the desk or through the slot by the front door at any time. The reading group meets on the first Monday of each month, and this month they are talking about a novel set on a small island during a very long winter.

Good afternoon come on in. Take whichever chair suits you. I am the doctor who will be looking after you here from now on.
Thank you. I will have the one with arms. It is easier to get up from. That walk from the car pk took more out of me than I expected.
take a minute and get your breath back. There is no rush. Do you find this us alright.
My neighbor drove me over, so I just sat back and enjoyed the view. He has gone to the coffee shop downstairs. He swears this scones are with the trip on their own.
I will have to try one at lunch, so this is your first visit with us. I have read the letter from the hospital, but I would like to hear the story in your own words what happened.
I was in the hospital from sep1ird to sep1er seventh for about a week before that. My ankles had been swelling up and I was getting more and more breathless. The night before I went in, I had to sleep sitting up in my arm chair. because every time I lay down, I felt like I was drowning.
that must have been frightening what did they tell you was going on.
The said my heart was not pumping properly and fluid had backed up into my lungs. The gave me water tablets through a drip and I lost about nine pounds of fluid in four days.
was at the first time anyone had mentioned your heart.
it was I had trouble with my chest for years, the COPD, so I always put the breathlessness down to my lungs. My heart never crossed my mind.
That' is very common because both conditions feel so alike from the inside. Apart from your heart and your lungs have you had any other illnesses or operations.
I have had high blood pressure for about 20 years and I had a hernia repaired about 15 years ago. Other than that, I have been lucky.
and how has your breathing been since you came home.
better than before I went in but not back to normal. I can walk to the end of my road about 200 yards and then I have to stop and lean on a wall. Stairs are the worst. I get to the top of a flight and I am puffing.
it at night, how many pillows do you sleep on now.
two pillows before the hospital it was four and I still woke up gasping. I have not had one of those nights since I got home.
That's a real improvement any chest pain either at rest or when you are walking.
No no chest pain. I get a tight feeling when I am wheezy but that is different.
if you had any fainting or felt as if you might pass out.
No, I go a bit lightheaded if I stand up too quickly from the arm chair but I have never fainted.
what about your heart racing or fluttering, any palpitations.
none that I have noticed.
are you weighing yourself at home.
every morning like they told me to. When I left the hospital, I weighed 184 pounds and this morning I was 186. It is crept up a pound here and there, but no big jumps.
keeping a record like that is exactly what we need. How is the swelling in your legs these days.
much better than it was. By the evening, my socks leave a deep mark around my ankles but in the morning it is mostly gone.
Let's turn to your chest when were you diagnosed with COPD.
about eight years ago. I smoked 20 a day for 40 years and I stopped the week they told me about my lungs. I haven' touched one since.
Well done, that's the hardest thing anyone can do for their lungs. were you around a lot of dust at work.
I was in the building trtraade all my working life. Plastered dust and cement every day and nobody wore a mask back then.
u many flare-ups if you had in the last year.
had two flare-ups both last winter. each time my old doctor gave me a course of prednisone and an antibiotic and I got over it at home. I have never been admitted for my chest.
You cough most days, are you bringing anything up.
Most mornings I cough up a bit of white phlegm about a teaspoon and then it settles. It has not changed color lately.
any fever or chills recently.
no nothing like that.
Then let's go through your medicines one by one. I see you brought them all in a bag, which is perfect.
every box in the house. The hospital changed so much that I have lost track of what does want.
We will sort it out together. This small white one is bisoprolol 5 mg once a day. It slows your heart a little and over time helps it pump better. How are you getting on with it.
I take the bisoprolol every morning with my breakfast. I have not missed a single day since I came home.
excellent. This one is sacubitril and valsartan 24/26 mg twice a day. It iss one of the most important medicines for a week heart when do you take it.
morning and evening 12 hours apart. The pharmacist at the hospital was very firm about that.
Good, then your water tablet. The discharge letter says furosemide 40 mg sorry 20 mg once a day in the morning. Does that match your box.
it does some days I take the water tablet at lunchtime if I am going out. So I am not hunting for a toilet or morning.
That's fine as long as you take it before 2:00 in the afternoon or you will be up all night. The other heart tablets are spironolactone 25 mg and e impagliflozin 10 mg both once a day.
I take both of those after breakfast with the bisoprolol. The pharmacist said the Empagliflozin looks after the kidneys as well.
it does in the heart too, now the inhalers which ones are you using.
the tterotropium two puffs every morning and the blue one the albuterol when I am short of breath. Can you refill my tiotropium inhaler. The counter says I have only got five days left.
Yes of course running out would set your chest back, so you will have a new one at your usual pharmacy by tomorrow, how often are you using the blue inhaler.
I use the blue one once or twice most days usually after the stairs. Before the hospital, it was five or six times a day.
show me how you take the tiotropium, perten for me just as you do at home.
I breathe out into it to empty my lungs, put my lips round and press and breathe in like that.
nearly perfect, breathe out away from the mouth piece because breathing into it puts moisture inside, then se your lips, press and take a slow deep breath and hold it for 10 seconds.
In all these years, nobody ever showed me that.
Plenty of people were never shown. Do you take anything you by yourself from a drug store or the supermarket or anything herbal.
just ibuprofen for my knees two tablets three times a day most days. My knees have grumbled ever since I retired.
Stop the ibuprofen completely please. It makes the body hold on to salt and water. It can strain the kidneys and it works against your heart medicines. For your knees, use acetaminophen instead up to 1 g three times a day.
I had no idea I have been buying it by the big box.
Most people don't know, it isn't printed on the box in large letters. Do you have any allergies to medicines.
just the one last winter and antibiotic for a chest infection gave me hives all over my arms and chest. It was doxycycline.
Thank you that matters. I will add doxycycline to the allergy list, so no one gives it to you again. T the hives settle quickly.
within a couple of days once I stopp taking it.
Let me ask about a few other things, how is your appetite and how much salt are you eating.
My appetite is not what it was. I have cut out the cryps in the bakon and I do nott add salt to the table anymore. I still have a take away on a Friday. I will admit.
W will come back to the take away how are your water works are you getting up at night to pass urine.
I am up twice a night to pass water now which is more than before the water tablet. The stream is a bit slow, but it always has been.
in your bowels, any black stools or bleeding.
know the regular as clock workor.
I am glad to hear it, how is your mood with all of this going on. It's a lot to take in.
I have my low days. I have lived on my own for six years now and the evenings can be long. but I have got good neighbors and I go to the bulls clalub on a Wednesday when my chest allows.
Thank you for telling me. Do you drink any alcohol.
a pint of bitter at the bows club and that' is my lot for the week.
that is sensible who helps you with shopping in your tablets.
My neighbor does a big shop for me on a Saturday. I sought my own tablets into a pillbox on a Sunday night so I can see at a glance if I have missed one.
That's a good system, how are you sleeping apart from the pillows.
about six hours a night and I wake up rested enough. Nobody has ever complained about my snoring, but then there is nobody there to hear it.
When did you last have a flu vaccine.
last Octoba at the chemist. I have never had the pneumonia one.
Let me examine you now. Could you sit up on the couch for me leaning back at an angle.
Give me a second that we go.
your blood pressure is 112/68, your pulse is 62 and regular, and your oxygen level is 93% on room air. Your weight on our scale is 187 pounds. Your heart sounds are regular and I can't hear a murmur. you don't have raise neck veins.

it' is lower because your heart medicines are doing their job and for your heart that's a good number. I have also gone through the results of the hospital passed on to us.
go on then I would like to know where I stand.

a third that doesn' sound like much at all.
it's low, but it isn't a fixed number. You can see it climb over the next few months if the medicines are taken every day, so let me put it all together for you.
please do I have been handed so many bits of paper that I can't see the whole picture.

. That is a lot less teath than I am used to and the take away.

what about that low salt stuff they cell in the supermokeet.
